subtitles.en: In 1988, George Bush has candidate at the convention in a speech written by Peggy Noonan who wrote speeches from Ronald Reagan. She said the biggest takeaway from the convention is when George Bush said, read my lips, no new taxes.
subtitles.zh: 1988年，乔治·布什作为候选人在大会上发表由佩吉·努南撰写的演讲，她曾为罗纳德·里根写稿。她说大会最大的亮点是布什说：“读我的唇，不加新税。”

subtitles.en: 1990, as president, George Bush raised taxes and nathmath to the Republican Party, typically doesn't raise taxes.
subtitles.zh: 1990年，作为总统，乔治·布什加税了，这对通常不加税的共和党来说很不寻常。

subtitles.en: Because the interest on the debt reached a record level back then, 3.2% of GDP. So that trillion dollars, David, that you mentioned, is 3.2% of GDP.
subtitles.zh: 因为当时债务利息达到创纪录水平，占GDP的3.2%。所以你提到的那1万亿美元，大卫，就是GDP的3.2%。

subtitles.en: So we're back to that level for the first time likely to reach 4% by the end of the decade.
subtitles.zh: 所以我们首次回到那个水平，到本十年末可能达到4%。

subtitles.en: So the read my lips moment is in 2029, when a president has to do something that's in nathma to his or her party, one final note on it, Bill Clinton did as well.
subtitles.zh: 所以“读我的唇”时刻在2029年，届时总统必须做一些对其政党来说不寻常的事，最后一点，比尔·克林顿也这么做了。

subtitles.en: He cut the capital gains tax rate, even though raised the top tax rate, but it's been fluctuating for 40 years in the high thirties, no big deal, really.
subtitles.zh: 他降低了资本利得税率，尽管提高了最高税率，但40年来一直在30%多的高位波动，其实没什么大不了的。

subtitles.en: So he did something in nathma to the party. The actions by those two presidents led to four years of budget surpluses eventually by the end of the 1990s.
subtitles.zh: 所以他做了对其政党不寻常的事。这两位总统的行动最终在90年代末带来了四年的预算盈余。

subtitles.en: So we need a president in a read my lips moment in 2029, when taking office, to do something different than the party might expect, because this is the only way to tackle this problem, to do something unusual.
subtitles.zh: 所以我们需要一位总统在2029年上任时迎来“读我的唇”时刻，做一些政党可能意想不到的事，因为这是解决这个问题的唯一途径，做一些不寻常的事。

subtitles.zh: 本周根据司法部公布的细节，拉哈姆·阿尔福森已于上周被捕。

subtitles.en: He was a employee in the product team in open AIs, headquarters in San Francisco.
subtitles.zh: 他曾是OpenAI旧金山总部产品团队的员工。

subtitles.en: What emerged is that he has also been charged on planting a secret recording device.

subtitles.en: What kind of emerged through details released by the Justice Department was this recording device was discovered in one of the conference rooms and it was plugged into the back of the TV.
subtitles.zh: 司法部公布的细节显示，该录音设备是在一间会议室里被发现的，插在电视背面。

subtitles.en: Almost disguised, it was covered in toilet paper.

subtitles.en: They haven't been able to find out what the recording device was trying to do because its contents were encrypted.

subtitles.en: But I think what is interesting about this is the Justice Department said that chatbot logs associated with an account by Abdul Rahm and Spouse had had details where someone had been asking the chatbot for advice on how to install a recording device like this and also how to use cases.
subtitles.zh: 但有趣的是，司法部表示，与阿卜杜勒·拉赫姆及其配偶账户相关的聊天机器人日志显示，有人曾向聊天机器人咨询如何安装此类录音设备以及使用场景。

subtitles.en: Katrina Mulligan, who is a senior member of open AIs national security team, estimated that just half of the 300 top AI researchers in the world are American.

subtitles.en: And this presents a problem. There's this balance between wanting to keep this technology secure in a race where the easiest way to catch up is to just steal it.
subtitles.zh: 这带来了一个问题：在希望保持技术安全的竞赛中，追赶的最简单方式就是窃取。

subtitles.en: Is this going to become a harder and harder debate because these skills are lacking here in the U.S. But they have to be careful with who they're hiring.
subtitles.zh: 由于美国缺乏这些技能，这场辩论是否会越来越激烈？但他们必须谨慎选择雇佣对象。

subtitles.en: Yeah, and this is interesting because this person who has been arrested, he's a Saudi national. He's been a resident in the U.S. since 2020 and has been a lot of attention paid to his nationality and also to the fact that he himself has talked openly about advising Saudi government agencies about their technology use.
subtitles.zh: 是的，有趣的是，被捕者是沙特国民，自2020年起居住在美国。他的国籍以及他公开谈论为沙特政府机构提供技术使用建议一事，引发了大量关注。

clips.speaker: Morgan Meager
clips.title: 硅谷防谍训练：擦白板、防美人计，AI竞赛下的商业窃密焦虑
title_lines: AI竞赛下的商业窃密焦虑

subtitles.en: His lawyer has stressed that he has not been charged with acting as a foreign agent. He's just been charged with planting this recording device.
subtitles.zh: 他的律师强调，他并未被控充当外国代理人，仅被控安装该录音设备。

subtitles.en: I mean, it kind of, this case kind of comes in this moment in Silicon Valley where people are on edge.
subtitles.zh: 这起案件发生在硅谷人心惶惶的时刻。

subtitles.en: I mean, even before this incident, open AI had been advising its employees to look out for people trying to steal company secrets, so they had been running training sessions telling employees to wipe the whiteboards in case cleaning staff had been compromised.
subtitles.zh: 即便在此事件之前，OpenAI就一直建议员工警惕试图窃取公司机密的人，还开展培训，告诉员工擦干净白板，以防清洁人员被策反。

subtitles.en: They'd been advising employees how to look out for honeypot traps in and also. Yeah, I loved that when it was like if a woman is hitting on you, it's probably not because of you. Like think about where you work.
subtitles.zh: 他们还建议员工提防美人计陷阱。我喜欢那句：如果有女性搭讪你，很可能不是因为你本人，想想你在哪儿工作。

subtitles.en: It was a little abrupt, but yeah, they were like, basically, does she think you're cute or is she a spy? It gave me like World War II, you know, V for Victory, poster vibes.
subtitles.zh: 有点突兀，但基本上他们是在问：她是觉得你可爱，还是间谍？这让我想起二战时‘胜利’海报的感觉。

subtitles.en: Yeah, so I mean, this kind of reveals the attention that this was kind of expected that people were expecting people to be trying to take company secrets and this comes after, in January, a former Google employee was charged for stealing Google secrets and he was actually found in that case to be secretly working for two Chinese companies which, and he's sought to have stolen the information to benefit these two companies.
subtitles.zh: 这揭示了人们的警觉，他们预料到会有人试图窃取公司机密。此前在1月，一名前谷歌员工被控窃取谷歌机密，该案发现他秘密为两家中国公司工作，并试图窃取信息以利于这两家公司。

subtitles.en: And then even going back a bit further, I mean, in 2022, another Saudi national was charged working for, he was employed by X at the time for stealing company secrets.
subtitles.zh: 再往前看，2022年另一名沙特国民被控窃取公司机密，当时他受雇于X。

subtitles.en: So, I mean, industrial espionage is not new, but I think when it clashes with this hyper-competitive AI space, I mean, people are worried. Of course, these are top tech companies.
subtitles.zh: 商业间谍并非新鲜事，但当它与竞争激烈的AI领域碰撞时，人们确实担忧。当然，这些都是顶级科技公司。

subtitles.en: I want to get to your new piece that you have coming out. It's about who is training the AI models, okay? So it used to be digital equivalent of blue collar workers. That's kind of how do you say it, but how is it changing?
subtitles.zh: 我想谈谈你即将发表的新文章，关于谁在训练AI模型。过去这相当于数字蓝领工作，现在如何变化？

subtitles.en: Yeah, so I think we have this impression. People think about data workers as kind of low wage work. We're more familiar with this idea of Amazon Mechanical Turk, which is this very famous American platform.
subtitles.zh: 是的，我们有一种印象，认为数据工作者是低薪工作。我们更熟悉亚马逊Mechanical Turk这个著名的美国平台。

subtitles.en: It has been running for over 21 years and people were employed through the platform. They did kind of things like click on the cat in the photo, click on the car in the photo and they'd earn a couple of cents per task.
subtitles.zh: 它已运行超过21年，人们通过该平台受雇，做诸如点击照片中的猫、点击照片中的车之类的工作，每项任务赚几美分。

subtitles.en: And so this is what data work has been known for, but there's really these shifts going on in the data industry and that's signified by the fact that Amazon Mechanical Turk actually shut down last month.
subtitles.zh: 这就是数据工作的传统印象，但数据行业正在发生转变，标志就是亚马逊Mechanical Turk上月关闭。

subtitles.en: And so in its place, we're kind of seeing these new data companies. A lot of them are focusing or say they're focusing on white collar work. So they're focusing on so called experts.
subtitles.zh: 取而代之的是新型数据公司，许多专注于或声称专注于白领工作，即所谓的专家。

subtitles.en: These experts, they're not purely data workers. They might be doing data work on the side of their other job. So I spoke to you for this story, a radiologist, Annie Bricksey.
subtitles.zh: 这些专家并非纯粹的数据工作者，他们可能在主业之外兼职做数据工作。我为此采访了放射科医生安妮·布里克斯。

subtitles.en: And she does radiology full time and she works at a hospital. And then in her spare time, she is training AI models because she thinks that AI models can help her profession deal with an ever-increasing demand for scans.
subtitles.zh: 她全职在医院做放射科工作，业余时间训练AI模型，因为她认为AI模型能帮助她的行业应对不断增长的扫描需求。

subtitles.en: And so that's really interesting that we're seeing this influx of white collar workers enter this data work industry where we've really kind of had it associated with a different profile of labor before.
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，我们看到白领工作者涌入数据工作行业，而此前该行业与另一种劳动力形象相关联。

clips.speaker: Morgan Meager

subtitles.en: What's interesting here, though, is that they're using these experts to try to help them. But at some point, is it going to move past helping and start replacing the very experts who were training this?
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，他们利用这些专家来帮忙。但某一天，这是否会超越帮忙，开始取代那些训练AI的专家本身？

subtitles.en: I mean, I have a friend who used to do a lot of writing, she did script writing, she did comedy writing, and she has one of these jobs. She loves it. It's flexible. She just had a baby. She works from home.
subtitles.zh: 我有个朋友以前写很多剧本和喜剧，现在做这类工作。她很喜欢，时间灵活，刚生了孩子，在家工作。

subtitles.en: But it keeps saying to her, like, aren't you eventually putting yourself out of a job? Yeah. And I think that is a really big concern and people feel like this shift from kind of these more generalist tasks to these specialist tasks.
subtitles.zh: 但总有人问她：你最终会不会让自己失业？我认为这是一个很大的担忧，人们觉得这是从通才任务向专家任务的转变。
en_highlights: putting yourself out of a job

subtitles.en: People have worried this signifies AI models essentially absorbing larger amounts of human knowledge.
subtitles.zh: 人们担心这标志着AI模型本质上在吸收大量人类知识。

subtitles.en: And we've seen lots of predictions that AI models are going to make a lot of knowledge workers, people whose value rests on their expertise, they're going to push them out of the labor market.
subtitles.zh: 我们看到许多预测称，AI模型将让许多知识工作者——那些价值基于专业知识的人——被挤出劳动力市场。

subtitles.en: And we're not seeing that yet. But I think what's interesting is you kind of have these kind of two levels. So you have the expert workers. And then, but you still have kind of generalist data workers earning much lower wages.
subtitles.zh: 目前尚未看到这种情况。但有趣的是存在两个层级：专家工作者，以及收入低得多的通才数据工作者。

subtitles.en: They haven't disappeared. They're still there. But their work is also shifting. So I spoke to someone, Brooke Hansen, when she started, she started kind of decade ago doing this work. It was very easy.
subtitles.zh: 他们并未消失，仍然存在，但工作也在变化。我采访了布鲁克·汉森，她大约十年前开始做这类工作，当时很容易。

subtitles.en: She could do it when she was looking after her babies as a stay-at-home mum and just kind of quickly do it. But now it's changed in a way where it demands a lot more deep and focused work.
subtitles.zh: 她作为全职妈妈照顾孩子时就能快速完成。但现在变了，需要更深入、更专注的工作。

subtitles.en: And I think that's interesting that we have these kind of two levels running parallel to each other. And it's kind of like the data work industry is widening and absorbing.
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，这两个层级并行运行。数据工作行业正在扩大和吸收。

subtitles.en: And we don't yet know what the consequences of that are going to be on the labor market. But people are worried that it's going to warp the labor market in interesting ways.
subtitles.zh: 我们尚不知道这对劳动力市场的影响。但人们担心它会以有趣的方式扭曲劳动力市场。

反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
